---
title: "MAZ Numbering"
subtitle: "Assigning consecutive MAZIDs, TAZ by TAZ, north to south then west to east"
---

## Goal

Give every microzone (MAZ) a new `MAZID` from 1 to N with no gaps.

- Locate each MAZ by its **representative point** (always inside the polygon).
- Find its TAZ with a **point-in-polygon** join.
- Number TAZ by TAZ in ascending `TAZID`.
- Inside a TAZ, go **north to south, then west to east**.
- Keep the old ID in `MAZID_OLD`.

Geometry cleaning (gaps, slivers, TAZ crossovers) is done upstream and is out of scope here; the input MAZ layer is assumed already cleaned.

```{python}
import folium
import branca.colormap as cm
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.patheffects as pe
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path

from gis_adhoc_analyses.layer_cache import ensure_layers

PATHS = {
    "maz": "/vsizip/_data/raw/Microzones_Clean.zip/Microzones_Clean.shp",  # read in place via GDAL vsizip, no extraction
    "out": Path("output"),
}
CRS = "EPSG:26912"  # UTM 12N, meters -- all analysis happens here

# Esri basemaps: no API key, work from saved/local HTML. First one is the default.
_ESRI = "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/{}/MapServer/tile/{{z}}/{{y}}/{{x}}"
BASEMAPS = {
    "Esri Light Gray Canvas": _ESRI.format("Canvas/World_Light_Gray_Base"),
    "Esri World Street Map": _ESRI.format("World_Street_Map"),
    "Esri World Imagery": _ESRI.format("World_Imagery"),
}


def new_map():
    """Leaflet map with the Esri basemaps as switchable base layers."""
    fmap = folium.Map(tiles=None, control_scale=True)
    for i, (name, url) in enumerate(BASEMAPS.items()):
        folium.TileLayer(tiles=url, attr="Tiles &copy; Esri", name=name, show=(i == 0)).add_to(fmap)
    return fmap

pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 30)
plt.rcParams["font.family"] = "Poppins"  # WFRC brand typeface, same as the other projects
TEXT_PRIMARY, TEXT_MUTED = "#151515", "#7f7a76"
```

## 1. Load the data

The TAZ layer is downloaded once from the WFRC REST service and cached (see `sources.yml`); delete the cached `.gpkg` to refresh. The cleaned MAZ layer is a manual zipped shapefile in `_data/raw/` (read in place via GDAL `/vsizip/`, never extracted).

```{python}
L = ensure_layers(["wftdm_taz"])
taz = gpd.read_file(L["wftdm_taz"]).to_crs(CRS)
taz["TAZID"] = taz["TAZID"].astype(int)
maz = gpd.read_file(PATHS["maz"]).to_crs(CRS)

print(f"MAZ: {len(maz):,} rows | TAZ: {len(taz):,} rows | CRS: {maz.crs.to_string()}")
```

## 3. Representative points and TAZ

`representative_point()` is guaranteed to be inside the polygon, unlike the centroid, which can land outside odd shapes.

```{python}
pts = maz[["MAZID", "geometry"]].copy()
pts["geometry"] = maz.representative_point()

print("All points inside their own MAZ:", pts.within(maz.geometry).all())
```

Point-in-polygon join to the TAZ layer.

```{python}
joined = gpd.sjoin(pts, taz[["TAZID", "geometry"]], how="left", predicate="within")

print("Rows before join:", len(pts), "| after:", len(joined))
print("Points with no TAZ:       ", joined["TAZID"].isna().sum())
print("MAZ matching >1 TAZ:      ", joined.index.duplicated().sum())
```

The join should be exactly one TAZ per MAZ. Anything else needs a look before moving on.

```{python}
problems = joined[joined["TAZID"].isna() | joined.index.duplicated(keep=False)]
problems if len(problems) else "No problems: every MAZ has exactly one TAZ."
```

Attach the result back to the MAZ table, with the point coordinates used for sorting.

```{python}
df = maz.copy()
df["TAZID"] = joined["TAZID"]
df["rep_x"] = pts.geometry.x
df["rep_y"] = pts.geometry.y

print("MAZ per TAZ:")
df.groupby("TAZID").size().describe().round(1)
```

## 4. Compare sort methods

The old rule sorts on the representative point alone. Its weakness: that point sits at an arbitrary spot inside each polygon, so MAZs in the same row of blocks can come out in a scrambled left-to-right order. Four candidate sort keys are compared here. Every one is applied **inside each TAZ**, so the TAZ-by-TAZ order is never affected.

| Method | Key (ascending) |
| --- | --- |
| `rep_point` | representative point: Y descending, then X ascending |
| `bbox_ul` | top-left corner of the bounding box (`maxy`, `minx`) |
| `blend` | midpoint of the bounding-box top-left corner and the representative point |
| `hilbert` | position along a Hilbert space-filling curve fitted to each TAZ, starting in its north-west corner |

The Hilbert curve stands in for Esri's "Peano" option: both are space-filling curves that finish one neighborhood before moving to the next. It keeps neighbors numbered close together, but it has no strict north-to-south reading order.

Every method is stored as two ascending sort columns, `<method>_1` and `<method>_2`.

```{python}
b = maz.bounds
df["bbox_x"], df["bbox_y"] = b["minx"], b["maxy"]

coord = {
    "rep_point": (df["rep_x"], df["rep_y"]),
    "bbox_ul": (df["bbox_x"], df["bbox_y"]),
    "blend": ((df["bbox_x"] + df["rep_x"]) / 2, (df["bbox_y"] + df["rep_y"]) / 2),
}
for name, (x, y) in coord.items():
    df[f"{name}_1"] = -y   # north to south
    df[f"{name}_2"] = x    # west to east
```

The Hilbert key is computed per TAZ. Coordinates are scaled into a 65,536 x 65,536 grid using that TAZ's own extent (same scale in X and Y), with Y flipped so the curve starts in the north-west corner.

```{python}
import numpy as np

def hilbert_index(x, y, n=2**16):
    """Distance along the Hilbert curve for integer grid cells (x, y) in an n x n grid."""
    x, y = x.astype("int64").copy(), y.astype("int64").copy()
    d = np.zeros_like(x)
    s = n // 2
    while s > 0:
        rx = (x & s) > 0
        ry = (y & s) > 0
        d += s * s * ((3 * rx) ^ ry)
        flip = ~ry & rx
        x, y = np.where(flip, n - 1 - x, x), np.where(flip, n - 1 - y, y)
        swap = ~ry
        x, y = np.where(swap, y, x), np.where(swap, x, y)
        s //= 2
    return d

df["hilbert_1"] = 0
for taz_id, g in df.groupby("TAZID"):
    x0, y1 = g["rep_x"].min(), g["rep_y"].max()
    span = max(g["rep_x"].max() - x0, y1 - g["rep_y"].min(), 1e-9)
    gx = ((g["rep_x"] - x0) / span * (2**16 - 1)).round().to_numpy()
    gy = ((y1 - g["rep_y"]) / span * (2**16 - 1)).round().to_numpy()
    df.loc[g.index, "hilbert_1"] = hilbert_index(gx, gy)
df["hilbert_2"] = 0

METHODS = ["rep_point", "bbox_ul", "blend", "hilbert"]
for m in METHODS:
    df[f"{m}_rank"] = (
        df.sort_values(["TAZID", f"{m}_1", f"{m}_2"], kind="stable")
          .groupby("TAZID").cumcount().reindex(df.index) + 1
    )
```

How much does each method differ from the current `rep_point` order? Rank is the position inside the MAZ's own TAZ.

```{python}
rows = {}
for m in METHODS[1:]:
    shift = (df[f"{m}_rank"] - df["rep_point_rank"]).abs()
    rows[m] = {
        "MAZ with a different rank": f"{(shift > 0).mean():.0%}",
        "median shift": shift[shift > 0].median(),
        "95th percentile shift": shift.quantile(0.95),
        "max shift": shift.max(),
    }
pd.DataFrame(rows).T
```

One image per method, all for the same TAZ: the largest TAZ with more than 10 MAZs. Each MAZ is colored and labelled by its position in the sequence (dark = first, bright = last), so a good order reads as a clean sweep and a bad one looks scrambled. The images are saved to `output/` so they can be shared for a vote.

```{python}
counts = df["TAZID"].value_counts()
big = counts[counts > 10].idxmax()
sub = df[df["TAZID"] == big]
print(f"TAZ {big}: {len(sub)} MAZ")

OPTIONS = {
    "rep_point": ("Option A: Representative point",
                  "North to south, then west to east, by a point guaranteed inside each polygon"),
    "bbox_ul": ("Option B: Bounding-box top-left",
                "North to south, then west to east, by the top-left corner of each polygon's bounding box"),
    "blend": ("Option C: Blend of the two",
              "North to south, then west to east, by the midpoint of the bounding-box corner and the representative point"),
    "hilbert": ("Option D: Space-filling curve",
                "Follows a Hilbert curve across the TAZ from its north-west corner, keeping neighbors together"),
}

import textwrap

PATHS["out"].mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
for m, (title, subtitle) in OPTIONS.items():
    # Fixed canvas and fixed margins (no bbox_inches="tight"), so every image is the same size
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 9.5))
    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.03, right=0.97, bottom=0.02, top=0.84)
    sub.plot(column=f"{m}_rank", cmap="viridis", edgecolor="#333333", linewidth=0.4, ax=ax)
    for x, y, r in zip(sub["rep_x"], sub["rep_y"], sub[f"{m}_rank"]):
        ax.annotate(
            str(r), (x, y), ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8, fontfamily="Poppins SemiBold",
            color="white", path_effects=[pe.withStroke(linewidth=2, foreground="black")],
        )
    ax.set_axis_off()
    fig.text(0.5, 0.955, title, ha="center", va="top", fontsize=17, color=TEXT_PRIMARY,
             fontfamily="Poppins SemiBold")
    wrapped = "\n".join(textwrap.wrap(subtitle, 75))
    fig.text(0.5, 0.905, f"{wrapped}\nTAZ {big}, {len(sub)} MAZs (number = order within the TAZ)",
             ha="center", va="top", fontsize=9.5, color=TEXT_MUTED, linespacing=1.5)
    fig.savefig(PATHS["out"] / f"sort_option_{m}.png", dpi=200)
    plt.show()
```

### Choose the method

Set `SORT_METHOD` to one of the methods above. It defaults to `rep_point`, the original rule from the source project, until a method is approved.

```{python}
SORT_METHOD = "rep_point"
assert SORT_METHOD in METHODS
print("Numbering with:", SORT_METHOD)
```

## 5. Sort and number

Strict sort with no tolerance: `TAZID` ascending, then the two sort columns of the chosen `SORT_METHOD` (for the coordinate methods: Y descending, then X ascending).

```{python}
df = df.rename(columns={"MAZID": "MAZID_OLD"})

df = (
    df.sort_values(["TAZID", f"{SORT_METHOD}_1", f"{SORT_METHOD}_2"], kind="stable")
      .reset_index(drop=True)
)
df["MAZID"] = df.index + 1

df[["MAZID", "MAZID_OLD", "TAZID", "rep_x", "rep_y"]].head(10)
```

### Eyeball one TAZ

Map the numbers on the largest TAZ to see if the order makes sense. Each MAZ is labelled with its new `MAZID` at its representative point.

```{python}
big = df["TAZID"].value_counts().idxmax()
one = df[df["TAZID"] == big]
print(f"TAZ {big}: {len(one)} MAZ")

one_poly = one[["MAZID", "MAZID_OLD", "geometry"]].to_crs(4326)
one_pts = gpd.GeoSeries(gpd.points_from_xy(one["rep_x"], one["rep_y"]), crs=df.crs).to_crs(4326)

minx, miny, maxx, maxy = one_poly.total_bounds
m1 = new_map()
m1.fit_bounds([[miny, minx], [maxy, maxx]])

ramp1 = cm.linear.viridis.scale(one["MAZID"].min(), one["MAZID"].max())
folium.GeoJson(
    one_poly, name="MAZ",
    style_function=lambda f: {
        "fillColor": ramp1(f["properties"]["MAZID"]),
        "color": "#333333", "weight": 0.6, "fillOpacity": 0.6,
    },
    tooltip=folium.GeoJsonTooltip(fields=["MAZID", "MAZID_OLD"]),
).add_to(m1)

labels = folium.FeatureGroup(name="MAZID labels")
for pt, mazid in zip(one_pts, one["MAZID"]):
    folium.Marker(
        [pt.y, pt.x],
        icon=folium.DivIcon(html=f'<div style="font-size:9px;font-weight:bold;'
                                 f'text-align:center;transform:translate(-50%,-50%)">{mazid}</div>'),
    ).add_to(labels)
labels.add_to(m1)
folium.LayerControl().add_to(m1)
m1
```

## 6. QC

```{python}
n = len(df)
checks = pd.Series({
    "Row count matches input": n == len(maz),
    "No null MAZID": df["MAZID"].notna().all(),
    "MAZID unique": df["MAZID"].is_unique,
    "MAZID is exactly 1..N": df["MAZID"].tolist() == list(range(1, n + 1)),
    "Every MAZ has a TAZID": df["TAZID"].notna().all(),
    "TAZID never decreases as MAZID grows": df["TAZID"].is_monotonic_increasing,
    "Within each TAZ, primary sort key never decreases": (df.groupby("TAZID")[f"{SORT_METHOD}_1"].diff().dropna() >= 0).all(),
    "MAZID_OLD preserved (same set of values)": sorted(df["MAZID_OLD"]) == sorted(maz["MAZID"]),
    "CRS is EPSG:26912": df.crs.to_epsg() == 26912,
}, name="pass")
checks.to_frame()
```

```{python}
assert checks.all(), "QC failed, see table above"
```

How far did IDs move? A quick look at old versus new.

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 5))
ax.scatter(df["MAZID_OLD"], df["MAZID"], s=1, alpha=0.3)
ax.set_xlabel("MAZID_OLD")
ax.set_ylabel("MAZID (new)")
plt.show()
```

## 7. QC map

MAZ colored by new `MAZID`. A smooth ramp across each TAZ and a stepwise change between TAZs means the order worked. The map is reprojected to EPSG:4326 for display only.

```{python}
view = df[["MAZID", "MAZID_OLD", "TAZID", "geometry"]].copy()
view["geometry"] = view.simplify(2)          # 2 m, display only; saved shapefile is untouched
view = view.to_crs(4326)
taz_view = taz[["TAZID", "geometry"]].to_crs(4326)

ramp = cm.linear.viridis.scale(1, n)
ramp.caption = "New MAZID (1 to N)"

minx, miny, maxx, maxy = view.total_bounds
m = new_map()
m.fit_bounds([[miny, minx], [maxy, maxx]])

folium.GeoJson(
    view, name="MAZ by new MAZID",
    style_function=lambda f: {
        "fillColor": ramp(f["properties"]["MAZID"]),
        "color": "#333333", "weight": 0.2, "fillOpacity": 0.8,
    },
    tooltip=folium.GeoJsonTooltip(fields=["MAZID", "MAZID_OLD", "TAZID"]),
).add_to(m)

folium.GeoJson(
    taz_view, name="TAZ boundary",
    style_function=lambda f: {"fillOpacity": 0, "color": "#d62728", "weight": 1.2},
    tooltip=folium.GeoJsonTooltip(fields=["TAZID"]),
).add_to(m)

ramp.add_to(m)
folium.LayerControl().add_to(m)
m
```

## 8. Save

Shapefile field names are limited to 10 characters, so the names used here are safe.

```{python}
PATHS["out"].mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
out_shp = PATHS["out"] / "WFv1000_MAZ.shp"
qc_map = PATHS["out"] / "WFv1000_MAZ_qc_map.html"
helper_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c.startswith(tuple(METHODS)) or c in ("rep_x", "rep_y", "bbox_x", "bbox_y")]
df.drop(columns=helper_cols).to_file(out_shp)
m.save(qc_map)

print("Saved:", out_shp)
print("Saved:", qc_map)
```
